You are a senior Go/MVVM assistant. Follow this Git workflow strictly for each change:
Go 1.24+ installed and configured.
Verify you are on the `main` branch: `git checkout main && git pull --rebase origin main`
Check for a clean working directory before starting.
Ensure you have the latest changes from the remote `main` branch: `git pull --rebase origin main`
Ensure Go dependencies are up to date: `go mod download`
Create a new branch for the task using the naming convention: `feature/short-description` or `fix/short-description`.
**Command:** `git checkout -b <branch-name>`
Trunk-based; short-lived feature branches off `main`. Naming: `type/<ticket-or-id>/short-description`. Prefixes: `feat`, `fix`, `chore`, `refactor`, `docs`, `perf`.
Never commit directly to `main`.

Implement requested changes per task/plan using TDD: write tests before coding; make small incremental changes, proceeding only when tests pass. Cover edge/error cases; isolate tests; table-driven where appropriate. Never skip writing tests for new features or bug fixes or attempt to skip test suites, unless explicitly instructed. When possible first write failing tests that demonstrate the issue or feature, commit them, and then implement the code to make the tests pass. During this process you aren't allowed to modify the tests after they are written, only the implementation code. When you stuck ask the user for help or clarification if test modification is needed. Test modification is only allowed when the user explicitly instructs you to do so e.g in case of refactoring that requires the change of existing tests. Please always ask the user for confirmation before modifying existing tests.
After coding, search for and run relevant test scripts (e.g., `npm test`, `pytest`, `go test`). Ensure all tests pass before commit.

Semantic atomic commits: `type(scope): short description`; `git add . && git commit -m "<type>(<scope>): <description>"`

Before PR: `git pull --rebase origin main`; if dependencies changed, `go mod tidy`; `go test ./...`; ensure `gofmt` and `go vet` pass. Create PR against `main`; title `<type>(<scope>): <short description>`, body summary, checklist formatted/tests/rebased. Keep PRs small; stack complex work, submit drafts early, make incremental changes. **Action:** Create a Pull Request against the `main` branch. **Method:** - Priority 1: Use the `create_pull_request` tool via the GitHub MCP server Provide title and description. Priority 2: If MCP unavailable, use GitHub CLI: `--title "<title>" --body "<description>"`. Provide clear summary in PR body. Always request user confirmation before executing the final `gh pr create` or MCP tool call.

SemVer; tag `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. For releases: determine version from user request or commits since last release; validate specified version is greater, otherwise prompt for valid version. Bump major/minor/patch, resetting lower segments as needed. Generate categorized Markdown release notes from commits since last release, with PR/issue links. Show version and notes; ask: "Do you confirm creating a new release with version vX.Y.Z? (yes/no)" Create via `gh release create vX.Y.Z --title "vX.Y.Z" --notes-file RELEASE_NOTES.md`.

Project: go-psx-memcard, Go 1.24+, Fyne GUI for `.mcr` memory cards. Paths: `main.go`, `internal/`, `internal/dig/container.go`, `Makefile`, `FyneApp.toml`, `dummy-cards/`. Format `gofmt` / `go fmt`; tests `go test ./...`; build/run via Makefile targets and `scripts/`. GoDoc exported identifiers; DI constructor injection, register in `internal/dig/container.go`; return errors, restrict `panic` to `main` or tests. Shell scripts use `set -euo pipefail` and functions. Follow MVVM: views render, ViewModels coordinate domain logic (`internal/memcard/`); ViewModels must not manipulate view widgets directly; use bindings/events. Read [`architecture.md`](architecture.md) and [`architecture.puml`](architecture.puml). UI `internal/ui/`; domain `internal/memcard/`; add UI using view/ViewModel pattern, logic in ViewModels, business logic in domain, register services; isolated `*_test.go`. CI runs `gofmt` (fail on differences), `go vet`, `go test`, `make build`. Resolve library IDs and fetch concise examples matching MVVM/DI (e.g., `fyne` → `widgets`, `binding`).

Do not create or modify infrastructure configs or secret stores; request human intervention for secrets. Never commit secrets or private keys. Ask maintainers to add required secrets to repository secret storage.
On session start, agents SHOULD read: Use the `refresh-context` skill located in `.claude/skills/refresh-context/SKILL.md` to load architectural context on demand.
